findings.title: Dark-theme badge-notification background no longer contrasts with its $secondary text
findings.body: .badge-notification keeps `color: $secondary`, but the new dark-theme background is `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`. In dark color schemes `$secondary` is the dark background color, so the text and background are both dark and the badge count can become unreadable. Previously the background was based on `$primary`, which is light in dark schemes and preserved contrast with `$secondary` text.

findings.title: Embedded-reply author link color uses inverted/wrong lightness values
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but it was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This makes the author link much lighter in light themes and much darker in dark themes, while comparable username links use 30% in light themes and 70% in dark themes. The result is poor contrast/inconsistent styling for `.topic-meta-data h5 a`.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the change uses 50% for both light and dark themes. The desktop equivalent uses 20% in light themes and 80% in dark themes. This reduces heading contrast/prominence on mobile and creates an inconsistency with desktop styling.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length values appear swapped relative to desktop
findings.body: Desktop modal uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` for the same hint text, preserving the original 70% light-theme value. Mobile now uses 30%/70%, changing the light-theme appearance and making the two views inconsistent. This looks like the light/dark values were accidentally swapped.

findings.title: Group member name color changed from 30% to 50% in light themes
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the change uses 50% for both light and dark themes. This alters the existing light-theme contrast and makes the name color identical to `.title`. If the intent was only to add a dark-theme equivalent, the expected pair would be 30% for light and 70% for dark.

findings.title: Mobile group member name color changed from 30% to 50% in light themes
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the change uses 50% for both light and dark themes. This changes the existing light-theme appearance and removes the visual distinction from `.title`. If this was not an intentional design change, the dark-theme replacement should preserve the original 30% light-theme value.

findings.title: Comment no longer matches the coldmap color implementation
findings.body: The comment says the default table cell color is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, but the surrounding styles now use `dark-light-choose(...)` with a secondary-based value for dark themes. The comment should be updated to avoid misleading future maintainers.
